e-9914.problem:
| $x$ | **$-6$** | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-7$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $8$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072172/assets/8002d38943a0f0b72e5c9cef2e3a455915479ca86c53ebe403b60a6b49f268a4.png)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which are the design matrix $X$ and the observation vector $\mathbf{y}$ in this context?
e-9914.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$\color{blue}-6$** | **$\color{blue}-3$** | **$\color{blue}-1$** | **$\color{blue}0$** | **$\color{blue}4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $\color{red}-7$ | $\color{red}-4$ | $\color{red}2$ | $\color{red}8$ | $\color{red}10$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 2 \\ 8 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

e-5610.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $10$ | $8$ | $6$ | $3$ |

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072172/assets/ba4b73a8acd1ede70da8d25a67159c74420ac2fd11d15c830a460071d881ff42.png)
*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.*
e-5610.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 8 \\ 6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
{\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{104}[\begin{aligned}26 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}27 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6.75 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y = 6.75 - x.$

e-5611.knowledge_point: Finding a Least-Squares Regression Line in Context
e-5611.problem:
An experiment consists of measuring how much a spring stretches (in inches) when one end of the spring is attached to the ceiling while a mass of $x$ ounces hangs from the other end. This data is shown below.

| Mass $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stretch $(y)$ | $0.8$ | $1.8$ | $3.2$ | $4.2$ |

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, how much will the spring stretch if we use an $8$-ounce mass, assuming that the trend continues?  

*Hint: You can use the fact that* 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072172/assets/400621e90f0419646dcd9e2b2e1bc31bc3cc280bef2be6c3d330c8b69308429c.png)
*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.*
e-5611.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system  

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0.8 \\ 1.8 \\ 3.2 \\ 4.2\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
{\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}23 & -6 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 \\ 38.2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.04 \\ 0.82\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y = 0.04+ 0.82x.$

Finally, to predict how much the spring will stretch if an $8$-ounce mass is hung from it,  we substitute $x=8$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.04+0.82(8) \\  & =6.6\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, according to the model, if an $8$ ounce mass is hung on the spring, the spring will stretch $6.6$ inches. 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=8$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

EXPLANATION
x −5 0 5 10 15
y 15 10 5 0 −5

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 10 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 2
?
x −2 −1 0 1 2
y −6 −5 −1 1 1

The vector of coefficients of the line y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

a
[11111]
b
[−2−1012]
c
[−6−5−111]
d
[−6−5−111]
e
[−2−1012]
Submit

decision.explanation: The observation vector is the column vector of measured y-values in table order: −6, −5, −1, 1, 1. This is option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

EXPLANATION
x −2 −1 0 1 2
y −6 −5 −1 1 1

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[1−21−1101112]⏞X[β0β1]⏞β=[−6−5−111]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that y is the column vector of observations −6, −5, −1, 1, 1, matching option d. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $4$ | $5$ | $8$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $4$ | $5$ | $8$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ 5 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the line y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

a
[1174−1−5]
b
[−5−14711]

[−8−6−4−20]

[−5−14711]

[−8−6−4−20]

EXPLANATION
x −8 −6 −4 −2 0
y −5 −1 4 7 11

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[1−81−61−41−210]⏞X[β0β1]⏞β=[−5−14711]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that y is the column vector of observations −5, −1, 4, 7, 11, matching option b. Option d is a row vector and has the wrong dimensions for the regression formula.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-8$** | **$-6$** | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $7$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-8$** | **$-6$** | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $7$ | $11$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 \\ 1 & -6 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 7 \\ 11\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 5
?
x −3 −2 −1 0 1
y −8 −4 2 6 10

The vector of coefficients of the line y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[11111−3−2−111]
b
[−3−2−101−8−40610]
c
[−8−3−4−22−160101]
d
[1−31−21−11011]
e
[1−81−41216110]
Submit

decision.explanation: For y = β₀ + β₁x, each row of X is [1, xᵢ]. Using x = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1 gives the matrix in option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-8$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-8$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -4 \\ 2 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

x −3 −2 −1 0 1
y −8 −4 2 6 10

The vector of coefficients of the line y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as

[β0β1]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[11111−3−2−111]
b
[−3−2−101−8−40610]
c
[−8−3−4−22−160101]
d
[1−31−21−11011]
e
[1−81−41216110]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION
x −3 −2 −1 0 1
y −8 −4 2 6 10

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[1−31−21−11011]⏞X[β0β1]⏞β=[−8−42610]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-8$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-8$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -4 \\ 2 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $5$ | $8$ | $10$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 8 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation 

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7.5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=7.5+3x.$

after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $5$ | $3$ | $2$ | $-3$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector. 

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=3-2.5x.$

before.html:
Question 8
?
x 0 1 2 3 4
y 6 4 3 1 −1

Find the line of the form y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above.

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=110[6−2−21],XTy=[139], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a
y=1.7−6x
b
y=6−1.7x
c
y=−1.7+6x
d
y=−6+1.7x
e
y=−1.7−6x
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients are β₀ = (6·13 − 2·9)/10 = 6 and β₁ = (−2·13 + 9)/10 = −1.7. Thus the best-fit line is y = 6 − 1.7x.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $6$ | $4$ | $3$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 9\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}13 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1.7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=6-1.7x.$

| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $5$ | $7$ | $12$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{56}[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ 28\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system  

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 7 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{56}[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}25 \\ 28\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6.25 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=6.25+2x.$

| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 14\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1.4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=2+1.4x.$

before.html:
Question 11
?

A statistician collected data on the height above the ground (in hundreds of meters) of a hot air balloon during the first five minutes of its flight. This data is shown below.

Time (x) 1 2 3 4 5
Height (y) 1.6 3.0 4.6 6 7.6

Find the line of the form y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the balloon's height after 6 minutes, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=110[11−3−31],XTy=[22.883.4], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a
906 meters
b
872 meters
c
868 meters
d
902 meters
e
826 meters
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients are β₀ = (11·22.8 − 3·83.4)/10 = 0.06 and β₁ = (−3·22.8 + 83.4)/10 = 1.5. Thus y = 0.06 + 1.5x. At x = 6, y = 9.06 hundreds of meters, or 906 meters.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
A statistician collected data on the height above the ground (in hundreds of meters) of a hot air balloon during the first five minutes of its flight. This data is shown below. 

| Time $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Height $(y)$ | $1.6$ | $3.0$ | $4.6$ | $6$ | $7.6$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the balloon's height after $6$ minutes, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1.6 \\ 3.0 \\ 4.6 \\ 6 \\ 7.6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.06 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.06+1.5x.$

Finally, to predict the height of the balloon after $6$ minutes, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.06+1.5(6) \\  & =9.06\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the balloon's height after $6$ minutes will be $906$ meters.  

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

XTXβ^=XTy.

before.name: Question 12
before.problem:
A bungee jumping instructor measures how much a bungee rope stretches (in meters) when one end of the rope is attached to the bridge railing while a weight of $x$ kilograms is hung on the other. This data is shown below.

| Weight $(x)$ | **$10$** | **$20$** | **$30$** | **$40$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stretch $(y)$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $2.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, how much will the rope stretch if the instructor uses a $65$-kilogram mass, assuming the trend continues?  

*Hint: You can use the fact that* 

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{500}[\begin{aligned}750 & -25 \\ -25 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 200\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

content.problem:
A bungee jumping instructor measures how much a bungee rope stretches (in meters) when one end of the rope is attached to the bridge railing while a weight of $x$ kilograms is hung on the other. This data is shown below.

| Weight $(x)$ | **$10$** | **$20$** | **$30$** | **$40$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stretch $(y)$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $2.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, how much will the rope stretch if the instructor uses a $65$-kilogram mass, assuming the trend continues?  

*Hint: You can use the fact that* 

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{500}[\begin{aligned}750 & -25 \\ -25 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 200\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
content.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 10 \\ 1 & 20 \\ 1 & 30 \\ 1 & 40\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.5 \\ 2 \\ 2.5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{500}[\begin{aligned}750 & -25 \\ -25 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ 200\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.5 \\ 0.05\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.5+0.05x.$

Finally, to predict how much the rope will stretch if a $65$-kilogram mass is hung from it, we substitute $x=65$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.5+0.05(65) \\  & =3.75\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the rope will stretch $3.75$ meters if a $65$-kilogram mass is hung from it.

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=65$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

content.problem:
The relationship between the advertising budget and sales (both in millions of dollars) of a company per year over several years is shown in the following table. 

| Advertising $(x)$ | **$2$** | **$2.5$** | **$3$** | **$3.5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sales $(y)$ | $10$ | $12$ | $16$ | $20$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the total sales when the annual advertising budget is equal to $$5$ million, assuming the trend continues? 

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}31.5 & -11 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}58 \\ 168\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2.5 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 3.5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 12 \\ 16 \\ 20\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

 

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}31.5 & -11 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}58 \\ 168\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4.2 \\ 6.8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-4.2+6.8x.$ 

Finally, to predict the value of the sales when the advertising budget is equal to $$5$ million, we substitute $x=5$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4.2+6.8(5) \\  & =29.8\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the total sales when the advertising budget equals $$5$ million will be $$29.8$ million. 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=5$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

A company collected data on the sale price (in thousands of dollars) of a particular used car model and the car's age (in years). This data is shown below.

Age (x) 4 5 6 7 8
Price (y) 12 10 8.5 7 6.5

Find the line of the form y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the sale price of a model that is 10 years old, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=110[38−6−61],XTy=[44250], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a
$2800
b
$4400
c
$4200
d
$3200
e
$3700
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients are β₀ = (38·44 − 6·250)/10 = 17.2 and β₁ = (−6·44 + 250)/10 = −1.4. Thus y = 17.2 − 1.4x. At x = 10, y = 3.2 thousand dollars, or $3,200.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
A company collected data on the sale price (in thousands of dollars) of a particular used car model and the car's age (in years). This data is shown below.

| Age $(x)$ | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** | **$7$** | **$8$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price $(y)$ | $12$ | $10$ | $8.5$ | $7$ | $6.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the sale price of a model that is $10$ years old, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}38 & -6 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}44 \\ 250\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 10 \\ 8.5 \\ 7 \\ 6.5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}38 & -6 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}44 \\ 250\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17.2 \\ -1.4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=17.2-1.4x.$

Finally, to predict the selling price of a car of the same model that is $10$ years old, we substitute $x=10$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =17.2-1.4(10) \\  & =3.2\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the sale price will be $$3\,200.$

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=10$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
